title: Unmask the spurious step-to-step masking edges in the `python` and `node` CI jobs, and re-measure the stale DATABASE_URL-gated test count
objective: In .github/workflows/ci.yml no step in the `python` or `node` job carries an `if:`, so GitHub's default `success()` makes a failing step SKIP every later step in the job, and a skipped step produces no evidence. A one-character formatting nit therefore silences the entire test suite in a job named 'Python lint, format, tests', and a Prettier difference silences every ESLint finding in `node`. Unmask the edges that are spurious while KEEPING the ones that are genuine install dependencies. Separately, a comment in the same file states a measured test count as present-tense fact with no date or command; re-measure it and restate it so it cannot silently rot.
materiality: CI gate correctness and a security-relevant disclosure route. `tests/unit/test_url_allowlist.py` asserts over the committed tree that every URL host is allowlisted, and it runs in the `python` job's `Pytest` step, so it is the SECOND CI route to the rule that keeps an internal hostname out of this public repository. Before this change a Ruff nit switched that route off.
evaluation_level_rationale: Touches a security boundary's CI enforcement route and changes when build-gating checks execute. Level 2 is mandatory for security boundaries under docs/AGENT_HARNESS.md.

measured_premise.derivation_method: Parsed .github/workflows/ci.yml and SIMULATED each step's effective `if:` against the outcomes of the steps before it. A masking edge is an ordered pair (A,B) in one job where B is `skipped` in a run in which A fails but would have run otherwise. Counted over steps carrying a `run:` key.
measured_premise.real_breakdown: 14 dependencies on an install step, plus `Validate secrets baseline` -> `Scan tracked files against baseline` in `secrets`, which is real for the reason documented on that step.
measured_premise.spurious_breakdown: python: Ruff lint -> {Ruff format check, Apply database migrations, Pytest}; Ruff format check -> {Apply database migrations, Pytest}; Apply database migrations -> Pytest. node: Prettier check -> ESLint.
measured_premise.disagreement_with_brief_stated_prominent: The task brief said 17 edges / 11 real / 6 spurious. MY MEASUREMENT: 22 / 15 / 7. The 17 is the SAME measurement restricted to edges whose MASKED step carries no explicit `if:`, which excludes the five deliberate install gates in `web`; that sub-population was reproduced exactly (17) as a cross-check. The 6-versus-7 difference is a genuine CLASSIFICATION difference, not a counting one: the brief left `Apply database migrations` -> `Pytest` undecided and asked for it to be settled on evidence, and the evidence settles it SPURIOUS.
measured_premise.instrument_negative_controls: The edge parser was proven capable of returning a different answer: stripping all `if:` raised the count 22->49; setting `!cancelled()` everywhere drove it to 0; unmasking one known edge dropped it by exactly 1; an unsupported condition RAISES rather than being silently counted as no-edge.

decision_migrations_to_pytest.evidence: Every integration module owns a module-scoped `engine` fixture that calls `command.upgrade(config, 'head')` ITSELF. MEASURED 2026-08-25 against a reachable but EMPTY postgres:16-alpine with `alembic upgrade head` never run beforehand: `python -m pytest -q` reported 2859 passed, 3 skipped, exit 0. Pytest builds the schema it needs and does not consume the CI step's output.
decision_migrations_to_pytest.corroboration: With DATABASE_URL pointed at an UNREACHABLE port, `python -m pytest -q` reported 2602 passed, 3 skipped, 257 errors, exit 1 - so when the database is broken the suite still returns roughly 2600 independent verdicts rather than noise. That is the test that separates a real edge from a spurious one, and this edge passes it.
decision_migrations_to_pytest.contrast_kept_real: An install edge fails that test (pytest with no packages reports import errors only), and so does `Validate secrets baseline` -> `Scan`, which is documented on the step.

decision_always_vs_not_cancelled: `!cancelled()`, matching `web`, `dependencies` and `secrets`. They differ on exactly one input, a CANCELLED run, and this workflow sets `cancel-in-progress: true` on `ci-${{ github.ref }}`, so cancellation is routine. `always()` would write a green step into a dying run, which reads as 'the gate ran and passed'. NOT MEASURED: a cancelled run was not observed, so this rests on documented Actions semantics and in-repo precedent, not on measurement.
in_scope: .github/workflows/ci.yml - add `id:` to the two install steps and `if: ${{ !cancelled() && steps.<install>.outcome == 'success' }}` to the four steps carrying a spurious incoming edge
.github/workflows/ci.yml - re-measure and restate the stale '162 tests' comment

package-lock.json and apps/web/package-lock.json - `npm install`/`i`/`update`/`audit fix` are forbidden; only `npm ci` was used
Any application code. Step order, step names, `run:` bodies, `uses:` and `with:` are unchanged.
The 15 real masking edges, which are deliberately preserved
acceptance_criteria: The 7 spurious edges are removed and the 15 real ones remain, asserted by PARSING both files and diffing the step-condition maps rather than by reading the diff
Only the `if` and `id` keys differ anywhere in the file
For each unmasked edge: BEFORE the later step is `skipped` on the earlier step's failure; AFTER it RUNS
AFTER, an unmasked step can still FAIL on its own merits
AFTER, the JOB is still RED - unmasking must not turn a failing run green
AFTER, a clean tree is fully green
Every prediction recorded BEFORE the run that tests it
Both lockfiles remain entirely on registry.npmjs.org
verification_commands: npm ci && npm run format:check && npm run lint
negative_and_regression_tests: Edge parser: 5 controls, each of which must come out DIFFERENTLY from the baseline
Scope assertion: before-vs-itself must report zero differences; the declared spurious list must be a subset of the BEFORE edge set
Measurement: an UNREACHABLE database must produce a LOUD non-zero exit, not a silent skip
Lockfile host assertion proven to fire on a planted off-registry host
progress.md append-only proven by raw byte-prefix comparison plus a flipped-byte negative control
data_security_privacy_portability_z0: No schema, data, provider, Z0 or portability change. Security-POSITIVE: makes the `python` job's URL-allowlist route unmaskable by a lint or formatting nit. No security check is weakened, suppressed or relaxed; no `continue-on-error` is introduced, so no failing gate is converted to a pass.

demonstrations_observed.method: Three genuine BEFORE/AFTER pairs. Control files byte-identical across arms by `git hash-object`; BEFORE ci.yml == main's blob 124ced29, AFTER == slice blob aff7df68. All 14 byte-identity assertions passed. Every prediction written to PREDICTIONS.md BEFORE any branch was pushed.
demonstrations_observed.pair_A_lint_control: #89 BEFORE: Ruff lint failure -> Ruff format check / Apply database migrations / Pytest ALL skipped; Prettier check failure -> ESLint skipped. #90 AFTER, same bytes: Ruff lint failure -> format RAN success, migrations RAN success, Pytest RAN success; Prettier failure -> ESLint RAN failure. Both JOBS failure on both arms.
demonstrations_observed.pair_B_format_control: #91 BEFORE: Ruff lint success, Ruff format check failure -> migrations skipped, Pytest skipped. #92 AFTER: format failure -> migrations RAN success, Pytest RAN success reporting 2859 passed, 3 skipped. JOB failure. THE CENTRAL RESULT: job RED from a quote-style nit while the entire suite ran and passed.
demonstrations_observed.pair_C_migration_control: #93 BEFORE: migrations failure -> Pytest skipped. #94 AFTER: migrations failure -> Pytest RAN failure, reporting 2602 passed, 3 skipped, 257 errors - matching the local measurement exactly. JOB failure.
demonstrations_observed.clean_tree: #88: all five jobs success; Pytest 2859 passed, 3 skipped.
demonstrations_observed.job_still_red: Verified at JOB conclusion on all six control runs. Unmasking turned no red job green. `continue-on-error` remains absent.
demonstrations_observed.can_still_fail_on_own_merits: ESLint failure in #90; Pytest failure in #94.
demonstrations_observed.instrument_controls: All five expected job names asserted present in every one of the seven reads; a deliberately bogus step name returned <step-not-found> every time; mergeable state read before interpreting any conclusion (all MERGEABLE).

not_verified_stated_prominently: No CANCELLED run was observed, so `!cancelled()` versus `always()` is NOT measured - it rests on documented Actions semantics and on the three jobs in this file that already use it.
Only `pull_request` events were observed; `workflow_dispatch` and `push`-to-main were not tested.
The 'no database' arm of the 258 figure is a LOCAL measurement only, because CI always sets DATABASE_URL. Only the 'with database' arm (2859 passed / 3 skipped) was reproduced in CI, twice.
